subject: yc-safe-postmoney
note: Forks found while encoding the Post-Money SAFE (row encodings/legalese-2026-09) on 2026-09-04. None is materialised as an Interpretation field: each was resolved at encode time, with YC's own SAFE User Guide (Appendix II worked examples) as the authority for the resolution where it speaks, and the resolution is asserted against the guide's figures in cases/user-guide-appendix-ii.l4. The register format is l4-ide's specs/todo/single-instruction-demo/schemas/fork-register.schema.json, reused per SPEC.md §1 although the pipeline itself is not run. Citation kind 'authority' is used for YC's SAFE User Guide: the publisher's own explanatory document, which is the nearest thing a standard form has to an authoritative construction.

source.quote: “Company Capitalization” is calculated as of immediately prior to the Equity Financing and (without double-counting, in each case calculated on an as-converted to Common Stock basis): … Includes all Converting Securities

citations.cite: Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §2 “Company Capitalization”, second bullet
Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §2 “Converting Securities” — “includes this Safe”

readings.description: The definition is a fixpoint: the Safe's own conversion shares are in the denominator of the Safe Price that determines them. Read as the unique solution of the equation, which for cap-method Safes is base ÷ (1 − Σ PAᵢ/Capᵢ).

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q2, p. 20: “= 10,000,000 / (100% - 15%) = 11,764,705”

readings.description: Read “Converting Securities” as excluding this Safe's own shares (a pre-money reading), so the denominator is the pre-existing capitalisation.
readings.rejection_rationale: Contradicts the definition's own text (“includes this Safe”) and the User Guide's Appendix III, which states that including the Safe is “what mechanically ensures that the valuation cap expressed in the safe operates as a post-money valuation cap”.

taken.rationale: The closed form is the guide's own arithmetic; the encoding states the recursive definition in a comment and asserts on every case that the closed form satisfies it (SPEC.md ruling R6).

witnesses: cases/user-guide-appendix-ii.l4 Q1: 11,764,705 under the fixpoint reading versus 10,000,000 under the rejected one

source.quote: this Safe will automatically convert into the greater of: (1) the number of shares of Standard Preferred Stock equal to the Purchase Amount divided by the lowest price per share of the Standard Preferred Stock; or (2) the number of shares of Safe Preferred Stock equal to the Purchase Amount divided by the Safe Price

citations.cite: Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §1(a)

readings.description: With several Safes, which take method (1) and which (2) depends on the Company Capitalization, which depends on the partition. Iterate the partition until it is stable (at most one pass per Safe); the price and Company Capitalization are then mutually consistent.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q5, pp. 22–23: Investor B switches to the Series Seed price and Investor A's Company Capitalization is recomputed as (10,000,000 + 1,216,360) / (100% − 5%)

readings.description: Do what the guide does: compute all-at-cap, compare each Safe once against the resulting price, recompute Company Capitalization for the Safes that stay at cap, and stop.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q5, p. 23 — the procedure as printed

readings.foreclosure: The guide's procedure is a worked example, not a rule; it is not stable in general (a switched Safe changes the price the others were compared against). On the guide's own figures the iterated fixpoint lands on the same partition in two passes, so the two readings do not diverge there.

taken.rationale: The instrument's text gives a per-Safe greater-of; a state in which some Safe would do better on the other side is not what its text says. The case file evaluates `passes used` so a reader can see how many passes the guide's example needed (two).

source.quote_absent_reason: The form says nothing about rounding shares or prices; the quotation would be the absence of a sentence.

citations.cite: Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §1(a) and §2 — no rounding rule anywhere in the instrument

readings.description: Keep exact rationals throughout; round share counts down to whole shares once, at the end; report prices unrounded.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q2, p. 20: share counts printed as whole numbers (588,235 from 588,235.29)

readings.description: Round the option pool increase to the nearest thousand and prices to four decimals, then compute onward from the rounded figures, as the guide's tables do.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q2, p. 19: “Option pool increase: 1,695,000 shares; Series A price per share: $1.1144” — the exact figures are 1,694,570 and $1.11447

readings.foreclosure: Nothing in the instrument licenses rounding an intermediate; the guide's rounding is a spreadsheet convenience and it changes the new-money share count by 294 shares on the guide's own example. Asserted in the cases to within 0.05%, which is the size of the guide's rounding.

taken.rationale: Only whole shares can be issued; every other rounding is a choice the parties did not make.

witnesses: cases/user-guide-appendix-ii.l4 Q2: option pool increase 1,694,570 versus the guide's 1,695,000; new-money shares 4,486,425 versus 4,486,719

source.quote: the lowest price per share of the Standard Preferred Stock

citations.cite: Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §1(a)(1)

readings.description: The instrument takes the Standard Preferred price as an input it does not define. The deal supplies the round's convention: price = pre-money valuation ÷ (fully diluted after conversion + option pool increase), with the increase sized to a target post-closing pool. Closed form in the module header.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q2, p. 20: “Series A Price per Share = pre-money valuation / (total fully diluted shares post safe conversion + option pool increase)”

readings.description: Treat the Standard Preferred price purely as a found fact supplied at closing, with no round arithmetic in the encoding.
readings.rejection_rationale: True to the instrument but useless for the next-round deliverable: the price and the Company Capitalization are mutually dependent (SPEC.md §6.4), so a supplied price is either consistent with the conversion or wrong. The deal's `round` block makes the convention explicit instead (ruling R7).

taken.rationale: The round module is kept outside the instrument's sections and named as a convention the term sheet owns.

source.quote: the amount payable on the number of shares of Common Stock equal to the Purchase Amount divided by the Liquidity Price

citations.cite: Postmoney Safe — Valuation Cap Only v1.2, §1(b)(ii)

readings.description: The amount payable per as-converted share is what remains of the Proceeds after the §1(d)(i) senior claims and the §1(d)(ii) Cash-Out Amounts of the Safes that cash out, divided by the Liquidity Capitalization (which excludes those cashing out). With every Safe converting this reduces to Proceeds ÷ Liquidity Capitalization.

citations.cite: SAFE User Guide, Appendix II, Example 1 Q3, p. 21: “The per share cash consideration for all stockholders, if the safes convert, is $0.8901 ($10,000,000 divided by the Liquidity Capitalization of 11,235,293)”
Postmoney Safe v1.2 §1(d): the Conversion Amount is “junior to payments described in clauses (i) and (ii) above”

readings.description: Always Proceeds ÷ Liquidity Capitalization, ignoring cash-outs paid ahead.
readings.rejection_rationale: Double-counts the Proceeds paid out as Cash-Out Amounts whenever the portfolio is mixed; §1(d) ranks the Conversion Amount behind them. The guide has no mixed example, so no printed figure decides this.

taken.rationale: Follows §1(d)'s ordering; agrees with the guide where the guide speaks.
